Where it began

Lakshmipathy Balaji was born in Madras on 27 September 1981 and went to school at Chettinad Vidyashram before studying at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College. He made his debut for Tamil Nadu in the Ranji Trophy of 2001–02 and was picked for India the following year.

His first one-day international came against the West Indies at Vadodara in November 2002, and his first Test against New Zealand at Ahmedabad in October 2003.

The player

Balaji was a right-arm fast-medium bowler who found his best form in 2004. On the tour of Australia that January he played all ten matches of the one-day tri-series and took 13 wickets. Then, in the Test series in Pakistan that spring, he played all three Tests and took 12 wickets, the second most in the series, as India won.

In March 2005, again against Pakistan, he took nine wickets in a Test, including his best figures of five for 76. That series brought the last of his eight Tests. In all he took 27 Test wickets at 37.19 and made 51 runs with a top score of 31.

What made him special

Selectors trusted him for whole series at a time. In one-day cricket he played 30 matches for India, and in the 2012 World Twenty20 he took nine wickets in four matches. An injury in 2005 kept him out for more than a year, but he came back in 2007 and earned another one-day call-up in 2009 after helping Tamil Nadu to a Ranji Trophy semi-final.

His batting was more of a happy accident. Fifty-one runs in nine Test innings is not a lot, but a top score of 31 suggests that on the right day he could make the bowlers work for their last wicket.

Away from the middle

Balaji was a winner in the Indian Premier League. Playing for Chennai Super Kings in the first season, in May 2008, he took the competition's first hat-trick against Kings XI Punjab and finished with five wickets and the man of the match award. He won the IPL and the Champions League Twenty20 with Chennai in 2010, then the IPL again with Kolkata Knight Riders in 2012, beating his old team in the final.

After retiring from all cricket in 2016 he moved into coaching, first as bowling coach and mentor at Kolkata in 2017 and then as bowling coach at Chennai from 2018 to 2022, before carrying on with the Super Kings Academy.

And finally

He made his Test debut for India in Ahmedabad and took one wicket. He played his first Twenty20 international at his home ground in Chennai nine years later. It was a long way round to a home debut, but he got there.
